transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I came in because... my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. But I'm not. I know for a fact they’ve been watching my every move on the floor and changing the pallet counts on my sheets just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

It’s always the blue pallets they mess with, too. The really heavy ones. My brother actually used to build wooden ones in his backyard, just stacking them up by the chain-link fence until the city came out and fined him for it. He had this huge dog back then, a Rottweiler mix, that would just sit there chewing on the loose wood all day long. It got splinters in its gums once and the vet bill was ridiculous. 

But anyway, yeah... my husband told me I needed to talk to someone about everything, so here I am.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

I mean... yeah, sometimes. Like, if I'm down in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes, I'll hear this man's voice. Clear as day, he just says, "Nicole, check it again." And there is literally nobody near me. 

It happens a lot when I'm doing the laundry, actually. Which is already the worst chore because the dryer in our apartment building squeaks so bad. The landlord, Gary, he drives this massive red Dodge truck but he won't spend ten bucks to fix the stupid dryer belt. My husband tried to patch it up with duct tape once, but it just made all our towels smell like burning plastic. And towels take forever to dry anyway, especially those thick ones we got on clearance at Target... they take up so much space in the basket. 

But yeah, anyway, I hear that guy's voice telling me to check things even when I'm all alone.
Aside from the voices and the feelings about your coworkers, have you been experiencing any periods where your mood is extremely low or unusually high for weeks at a time?

Well, I don't know about weeks at a time, but yeah, some days I wake up and I just feel... fired up, you know? Like I've got this electric energy and absolutely nobody can slow me down. I get so much done. But then, if my husband even looks at me funny or asks one tiny little question about the kids or what time my shift ends, I just snap. I go off on him because it feels like he's trying to control me. 

He's always been like that, though, ever since we met at that bowling alley off Route 9. They had this arcade in the back with a broken pinball machine—the one with the Addams Family theme? I loved that game. I actually used to collect quarters in this old coffee can just so I could play it on the weekends. My mom hated that coffee can because it was Folgers and she only drank Maxwell House. She was so picky about her coffee. She’d make me walk to the corner store in the snow just to get her specific brand. The guy who owned the store, Mr. Patel, he always gave me free cherry Jolly Ranchers... 

Wait, what did you ask me again? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, I just get really keyed up and angry if anyone tries to get in my way.
During those times when you feel that 'electric energy' and get a lot done, how many days in a row does that feeling typically last?

I don't really know, honestly. I don't sit there and mark it on a calendar or anything. Maybe a few days? Sometimes it feels like longer, but time just gets weird when I'm like that. It's like when you're driving on the highway and you just kind of space out and suddenly you're three exits past where you were supposed to get off. That happened to me last Tuesday when I was trying to get to the grocery store. I had to loop all the way back around by the old fairgrounds. They used to have this amazing funnel cake stand there, right next to the Ferris wheel. My kids love funnel cake, but the powdered sugar gets everywhere. It's a nightmare to get out of the car upholstery, especially since my husband insists on keeping the car spotless. He spends hours on the weekends just vacuuming the floor mats. He even bought this special little brush just for the air vents... 

But yeah, I don't really keep track of how many days it lasts. I just know I feel like I'm running on a different battery than everyone else.
When you have those periods of 'electric energy,' have you ever had them last for at least a full week without needing to sleep much at all?

Yeah, actually, that does happen. There have been weeks where I'll sleep maybe three hours a night. I'll wake up way before my alarm even goes off, and I just feel totally fine, like I don't need any more rest at all to get moving. 

It's crazy because my alarm clock is this super old digital one I've had since high school. The numbers are that really bright, obnoxious red. I got it at a yard sale down the street from my aunt's house. She used to have the best yard sales, always selling off these weird little porcelain figurines she collected. She had hundreds of them, all lined up on these glass shelves that I was terrified of breaking when I was a kid. One time, my cousin Jimmy actually did knock one over—it was a little shepherd boy or something—and she chased him out of the house with a broom. Jimmy was always getting into trouble, though. He joined the Navy right out of high school just to get away from her... 

But yeah, I'll sleep for like three hours and feel completely ready to go for a whole week.
Are there times when you feel like your mood is completely normal, yet you still hear that voice or still feel like your coworkers are watching you and changing your pallet counts?

Yeah, definitely. There was this one stretch, maybe a few weeks, where things were actually pretty quiet. I was sleeping closer to normal, you know, not racing around like a maniac all the time. But even then, I still heard that voice telling me to check things. And I knew, I absolutely knew, they were still messing with my pallet counts. 

Pallets are so heavy, you know? Like, people don't realize how much wood goes into making just one of those things. I got a splinter from one once that went right through my glove. It was this cheap leather glove I bought at the hardware store on Main Street. The guy who works the register there, he always wears these ridiculous suspenders. Like, bright neon green ones. He says they're for visibility, but I think he just likes the attention. My uncle used to wear suspenders, but only the clip-on kind, and they were always snapping off and hitting him in the back. He had this old pickup truck that smelled like wet dog and peppermint... 

But yeah, even when my mood is totally fine and I'm sleeping okay, the voice is still there, and I know they're still trying to screw me over at work.
